headline: Connectome-constrained inferences are audited against unmeasured physiology and operation-induced functional error
label: Connectome Model Evaluation Audits
summary: Two preprints stress-test connectome structure-function claims, auditing operations on C. elegans and tuning physiology fairly across Drosophila wirings.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that conclusions from connectome-constrained models depend on evaluation choices. The Functional Preservation Score audits connectome operations (quantisation, alignment, transport, local plasticity writing) on C. elegans and related data as sources of functional error. A separate test tunes physiology fairly across Drosophila wirings and finds some structure-function claims robust while others reverse. New here is explicit treatment of unmeasured physiology and of connectome operations as inferential error sources. The remaining preprints share an emphasis on rigorous analytic method rather than connectome structure: censoring-aware survival reanalyses of public optogenetics data (Neuropixels, striatal seizures), fixed-size Spearman regulon networks for TCGA master-regulator analysis, and null-matched efferocytosis scoring in stroke transcriptomes. This framing is dominant rather than universal across the set.
